Q057.question_text: Find the equation of the normal to the curve \(y = x^3 - 3x\) at the point where \(x = 2\). Give your answer in the form \(y = mx + c\), with the values of m and c rounded to 1 decimal place. [WMA12 P2, 4 marks]

Q060.explanation: Use the general term formula \(\binom{n}{r} a^{n-r} (bx)^r\) M1 [1]. For \(x^3\), \(n = 5, r = 3, a = 2, b = -3\), so the term is \(\binom{5}{3}(2)^{5-3}(-3x)^3 = 10 \times 4 \times (-27x^3)\) M1 [1]. Evaluating the coefficients gives \(10 \times 4 \times (-27) = -1080\), so the exact coefficient is -1080 A1 [1].

Q065.explanation: Factorise the curve as \(y = x^2 - 4x + 3 = (x - 1)(x - 3)\), so it meets the x-axis at \(x = 1\) and \(x = 3\); between \(x = 3\) and \(x = 5\) the curve lies above the axis, so the area is the definite integral M1 [1]. Set up \(\int_3^5 (x^2 - 4x + 3) dx\) M1 [1]. Integrate term by term: \([\frac{x^3}{3} - 2x^2 + 3x]_3^5\) M1 [1]. At the upper limit: \(\frac{125}{3} - 50 + 15 = \frac{125}{3} - \frac{105}{3} = \frac{20}{3}\). At the lower limit: \(9 - 18 + 9 = 0\). The exact area is \(\frac{20}{3}\) A1 [1].

Q066.explanation: Divide both sides by \(\cos x\) to convert to tangent: \(\frac{\sin x}{\cos x} = \tan x = 0.5\) M1 [1]. The principal acute angle is \(\arctan(0.5) \approx 26.565^\circ\) M1 [1]. Tangent is positive in the first and third quadrants, so the solutions in \(0^\circ \leq x < 360^\circ\) are \(26.6^\circ\) and \(26.6^\circ + 180^\circ = 206.6^\circ\) A1 [1].

Q075.explanation: Set up the definite integral between limits 1 and 3 M1 [1]: \(\int_1^3 (3x^2 + 2x) dx\). Integrate using the power rule: \([x^3 + x^2]_1^3\) M1 [1]. Substitute the upper limit 3: \(27 + 9 = 36\). Substitute the lower limit 1: \(1 + 1 = 2\). The exact area is \(36 - 2 = 34\) A1 [1].
